EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 16, 2021

speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on
Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.10.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 16, 2021

limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
consideration at a future meeting.

All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Mary Ann Powers – Since the start of the pandemic, restaurants have been struggling to survive.
First they are told to shut down indoor dining They invest in heaters, tables, chairs, and tents only
to have the state and county ban outdoor dining. This happens even though they are NOT a
major source of spread of Covid-19. The average person runs a greater risk of catching the virus
by visiting a government building. Through all of these shutdowns, we have had pop-up food
stands on corners & major streets in our city. These places do not have the expenses that the
restaurants have, so they don’t have to charge what restaurants would charge for their food. They
do not pay rent for the sidewalks they block when they occupy them with their tents and grills.
There is no social distancing enforced at these food stands. Do they even collect and pay sales
tax? There are no restroom facilities for the staff or customers. Do they wash their hands? If there
are no facilities…. how do they manage? I realize that Governor Newsom signed legislation
allowing these sidewalk businesses. I see the street vendors in El Monte, the city of Los Angeles
and County areas. Why don’t I see them in Arcadia, Monrovia, or even Baldwin Park? What are
these cities doing differently? For the survival of our El Monte businesses, and the health and
well-being of our citizens, it is time to make our codes as strict possible and to vigorously enforce
the codes. Whenever the citizens of El Monte are asked what new things they would like to see
come to the city, restaurants are always in the top ten. Let’s do what we can to keep the few we
have, and perhaps that will encourage more to come.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 16, 2021

Irma Zamorano – Good evening Mayor and City Council my name is Irma Zamorano resident for
50 years and I’m concern about the treatment of the street vendors, I want to know what’s the city
guidelines on permits, the cost and how to obtain a permit. How can we make the process easier
for all without violence. It’s concerning to know that a Los Angeles County health inspectors came
to the city on his day off just to shut down vendors. To me that’s a personal attack on one
particular vendor. It’s not right to see health inspectors abusing their power by continuous
harassment, bullying and intimidation of street vendors there should be a better way to let
vendors know if their permits are clear and meeting all the requirements to operate before setting
up. It’s sad to see health inspectors be thugs by throwing their food away taking their equipment
which is unnecessary. Please look into this matter I know there’s always to side of the story but
we should refrain from violence its uncalled for and makes our city look good.

Evangelica Child – I am a Health Policy Liaison with Day One here in El Monte at the Jeff
Seymour Center. Currently, I and a fellow colleague Carly Lopez are working on a project called
Project Sticker Shock. What Project Sticker Shock is we partner with retailers in the city such as
liquor stores and grocery stores mostly small businesses, and we partner with them to place
stickers on multi-packs of beer or liquor that may be in the fridges of the store. The Stickers bring
awareness to adults who may be purchasing alcohol to minors and show them what they can be
penalized with such as 6 months in prison or a $1,000 fine and at times both. We are working on
this project with College students from around the area and high school students so that we can
decrease underage drinking in the area. Thank you for your time.

Cosmic J Menes – Good evening Mayor Palin and esteemed city council, As a 69-year resident
of our fair city I am writing today to speak about several matters. I witnessed the horrendous acts
that took place between our police officers and street vendors. I think it’s despicable that a
business operator would be allowed to assault a police officer, while I also think it’s terrifying how
our police officers responded to the assault. I hope the city council will take swift action to
address this matter…perhaps another thoughts and prayers event streamed online will make
quick work of solving this pressing matter, because nothing says “we’re taking action” like sitting
in front of a camera. Moving on to another important matter, I would like to congratulate our
newest monarch, Mayor Pro Tem Victoria Martinez-Muela, her royal highness! I’m thrilled she has
finally been recognized for all her hard work, including when she held a fake fundraiser for local
charities, hoarded the money during a pandemic, then parceled it out during her election, as
though she was making these “donations” from her own pocket. So in addition to a 5-0 vote to
appoint madam mayor pro tem, I hope our council will vote unanimously to investigate Queen
Victoria’s shady dealings. I am concerned that with so much institutional knowledge in her head, it
may have pushed out her common sense. Finally I would like to speak of none other than the
great Diva herself, La Gran Señora, Irma Zamorano. It seems that Irma hasn’t paid her debt to
our fair city, currently owing in excess of $2,000 for her campaign fees. I’m glad her promise to
save El Monte $338,000 by not holding a special election was kept—by appointing anyone else
but her to the vacant seat, but her royal grandness needs to cough up from her gullet the money
she owes our city ASAP, before El Monte is bankrupt from lawsuits due to police getting beat up
by food vendors, or however that all went down. Maybe residents can ask Irma what happened,
since she claims to have been there defending the poor street vendors, and most definitely not
stuffing herself with free tacos.

Councilmember Margaret Clark, City of Rosemead – [INAUDIBLE]

Ricardo Padilla – [INAUDIBLE]… I would like to congratulate Councilmember Mr. Martin Herrera
our new City Council Member [INAUDIBLE]. We are aware that this appointment was made
possible by the vote of three women on this Council and it was not done with an election process.
There were many candidates with great qualifications, education qualifications, of course as an
educator of much interest to me many years of service and many years of in the community but at
the end the process is the process and the rest is history. With that being said I want to share
with Councilman Martin Herrera will make all of his decisions based on what is best for El Monte
residents. It was nice to see that we had a neutral unbinding party in Mr. Herrera. I say this
because we know what the voters said in the last election when it came to members of Team El
Monte and again this appointment was made possible by three women Councilwoman Ancona,
  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 16, 2021

  Martinez and Puente. Remember that the public always remember us by the work that we do and
  the decisions we make. If you recall they even remember that girls don’t just want to have fun
  girls want to have fun and get things done and Mr. Herrera is so lucky to be a part of you he will
  learn a lot and trust me I know I speak from experience. I sit on a board made up of all men and
  one woman and it is the woman who brings the most educational experience as well as the most
  life experience to our board. Lastly, I was really troubled and blindsided by not getting
  information regarding the two hotels on Valley over by Baldwin Avenue that the City of El Monte
  is involved with that will serve homeless families. This is something that your City Manager in my
  opinion could and should have done a better job of handling. When I called my Superintendent
  he knew nothing about it. Members of the Community are concerned about what this is going to
  look like and they have many questions. I did see articles and pictures of your City Manager
  involved with food distribution if you are going to distribute food great but you do not have to brag
  about it just do it. This tells me she does have enough time to call our Superintendent about
  homeless families and motels and its impacts. Please give us a report if possible

  Cosme Jimenez – I have three items, number one I want to congratulate the new Councilmember
  Martin Herrera he is going to be indirectly he is going to be the swing vote. [INAUDIBLE].
  Number two I got a copy of making comments against Councilwoman Martinez and Mayor
  Ancona I know where this is coming from using my name close to my name playing games with
  the Council. I hope something could be done with the help of the City Attorney also the
  Councilmembers that can help us are Morales and Councilwoman Puente because it is not
  attacking them. So I am not saying that they are involved with this but I am saying they might
  have a clue like I have too where this is coming from. Number three is the street vendors the
  street vendors we have we need somebody at City Hall that they can talk too [INAUDIBLE]

  Howard Owens – Thank you for taking my phone call it is kind of frustrating being home. I would
  like to speak about the problem with the street vendors. They take taxes, health department
  things and everything else and the street vendors don’t have to do that and we have to keep our
  restaurants open. Other items I have here are cannabis how much are we paying in legal fees for
  cannabis when we first started this thing all legal fees were going to be taken care of by the
  cannabis people. I want to thank this Council for going ahead and appointing someone. I want to
  thank our new Councilwoman for stepping up to the plate and you guys appointing Mr. Martin
  Herrera and I congratulate him and welcome him to the City. We need to get into the Council and
  where we can get up and speak we have a lot of frustrated people out there that haven’t been
  able to this for a year and it would be nice if we could come one at a time and come to the City
  Council with our views with our problems and with our worries. I appreciate this and looking
  forward to coming out here and speaking in person and not trying to do it over the phone. Thank
  you very much.
